prompt:
TESSERA STYLE SHEET
1. Modern editorial paper collage: bold magazine composition, refined 2D motion design, photographed flat under soft room light.
2. One flat block-colour paper ground fills the frame: deep magenta. The ground is a single unbroken colour.
3. Subjects are black-and-white halftone photographic cutouts with rough white torn-paper edges: objects, machines, buildings, maps, coins, screens, vehicles, anonymous paper hands. Every cutout is a plain, unmarked object: calendar pages, documents, coins, screens and vehicles are blank and unprinted, with no lettering, numerals, symbols, liveries or marks on them. Every cutout is matte paper reflecting only the room light, with a plain blank face: coin rims, document faces, screens and vehicle sides carry no lettering, numerals or marks.
4. Diagram elements are flat matte paper shapes and ribbons, tape, rubber stamps, string and pins, stencilled arrows, paper bar charts, stacked sheets, grid paper, torn strips, hole-punched tags, paper clips, in cream, black, pale yellow or the ground's contrasting colour, with real paper texture and print dots.
5. One consistent light from the upper left; each paper layer casts a small soft shadow.
6. Layout: the headline chip owns the upper third of the frame and stays uncovered; subjects and diagrams occupy the lower two-thirds. When the frame opens on a previous composition, its elements slide off or are covered in the first second and the new headline lands on clear ground.
7. Headline typography: one extra-bold sans-serif in black or cream, printed on a cream or black paper chip: one line, no wider than a third of the frame width, with safe margins, the chip sitting clear of the subjects. Letterforms are accurate, complete and stable from the frame they appear in; the chip is printed once and does not redraw. When the beat marks a hero number, that number alone may be printed larger, up to half the frame width.
8. Compositions vary in scale from beat to beat: some show one oversized subject filling the frame, some a small subject alone on open ground, some several elements arranged as a diagram.
9. Motion: elements enter fast with slight overshoot and a stable landing, then hold a clear reading window; one strongest focus at a time; the camera is locked; movement starts on the first frame and a small loop continues at the end; no empty frames.
10. 16:9, exactly 5 seconds, one composition, at most one crisp cut.
11. Identity anchor: rough white torn edges on every cutout; small paper shadow from the upper-left light.

BEAT
Ground: deep magenta.
Subjects: a paper runway; a cutout aircraft.
Opens cold on the ground colour; the first subject enters on the first frame.
Action: The previous chip is covered as the strip becomes a runway torn short; a cutout aircraft rolls to the torn end and stops.
Ends holding on the runway.
This composition is oversized: one subject fills most of the frame.
Headline printed on a paper chip: "1.4 MONTHS". This is the hero beat: the number may print larger, up to half the frame width.

ON-SCREEN TEXT: "1.4 MONTHS". This string is printed complete and correct from its first visible frame and never changes. It is the only lettering in the frame.

AUDIO: One English narrator, warm, clear, natural, brisk but unhurried, never an advertising shout. Speak the following line exactly once, word for word, beginning on the first frame: "At that rate, the cash on hand covered one point four months.". No other dialogue. Light paper-slap and tape sound effects beneath the voice; no music.

integrated_multimodal_description: [Shot 1] Cinematic, modern editorial paper collage style. The scene opens with a flat, unbroken deep magenta paper background filling the frame, photographed under soft room light with a consistent light source from the upper left. On the first frame, a rectangular cream paper chip slides in quickly with a slight overshoot to the upper third of the frame, featuring the clean, stable, extra-bold black sans-serif text "1.4 MONTHS", where the number "1.4" is printed significantly larger, occupying nearly half the frame width. Simultaneously, a large, black-and-white halftone photographic cutout of a runway, featuring rough white torn-paper edges and a matte texture, slides into the lower two-thirds of the frame. The runway is a plain, unmarked strip of paper with no markings or lettering. A second cutout, a black-and-white halftone aircraft with matching rough white torn edges, enters from the side, rolling quickly along the paper runway with a slight overshoot before coming to a complete stop at the torn end. Both the runway and the aircraft are matte, reflecting only the soft room light, and cast small, soft shadows to the bottom right. The camera remains in a Static Shot throughout the 5-second duration. A male narrator (S1), with a warm, clear, and natural mid-range timbre and a brisk but unhurried speaking rate, speaks starting on the first frame: <d>[English] At that rate, the cash on hand covered one point four months.</d>

A crisp, rhythmic paper-slap sound occurs as the headline chip and runway land, followed by a short, sticky sound of adhesive tape being pressed down. A subtle, dry sliding sound accompanies the aircraft's movement across the paper surface.
